title: Chatbot Output Accuracy & Accountability Pattern
description: A pattern for grounding customer-facing chatbot responses in verified source-of-truth policy documents, with an accuracy-review and correction pathway, so the chatbot's statements are treated as accountable company communications rather than disclaimed third-party output.
problem: Customer-facing chatbots answer policy questions (refunds, eligibility, pricing) by generating free-text responses that can drift from the organisation's actual, current policy, with no review step before the customer relies on the answer.
solution: Ground chatbot responses to policy questions in a maintained, versioned source-of-truth document rather than open-ended generation; log every substantive policy statement the chatbot makes; and provide a fast escalation/correction path when a discrepancy is found, treating the correction with the same urgency as a human agent's documented error.
applicability: Any customer-facing conversational AI system that answers questions about pricing, eligibility, refunds, or other binding policy terms.
consequences: Grounding reduces but does not eliminate the risk of incorrect answers (source documents can themselves be ambiguous or stale); logging and review add operational overhead proportional to conversation volume.

citations.title: Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149
citations.publisher: Civil Resolution Tribunal of British Columbia

relationships.reason: Grounded, logged responses are a concrete way to meet the transparency/information-to-users obligation this control describes.
The pattern's output is a chatbot response accuracy audit log.
